```{r setup}
library(MFO)
```

This vignette follows one participant of the example data from the raw gas
exchange to the numbers you would report in a paper. Every intermediate
object is computed in plain R, so you can see each formula at work, and it is
checked against what `MFO()` returns. Every number in the text is computed
when the vignette is built.

## 1. What the test measures

Fat oxidation is not measured directly; it is inferred from oxygen uptake
(VO2) and carbon dioxide output (VCO2). Oxidising 1 g of glucose consumes
0.746 L of O2 and produces 0.746 L of CO2, a respiratory exchange ratio (RER)
of 1.00; oxidising 1 g of fat consumes 2.03 L of O2 and produces 1.43 L of
CO2, an RER of about 0.70 [@frayn1983, Table 1]. Solving these two balances
for the two unknowns gives the stoichiometric equations that turn VO2 and
VCO2 into grams of carbohydrate (CHO) and fat (FAT) oxidised per minute
[@frayn1983]. The package uses them with urinary nitrogen set to zero, i.e.
it ignores protein oxidation. The inference fails at high intensity, when
CO2 released from the bicarbonate pool to buffer lactate adds to the CO2
produced by oxidation [@jeukendrup2005].

In a graded test the participant exercises in steps of increasing intensity,
classically 3 min with 35 W increments [@achten2002]; @cheneviere2009 used
3 min with 20 W. Plotted against intensity, fat oxidation rises, reaches a
peak, the **maximal fat oxidation** rate (MFO, g/min), and falls towards zero.
The intensity at the peak is **Fatmax**, expressed as %VO2max. In the sample
of @achten2002 Fatmax was 64 %VO2max (74 %HRmax), and Fatmax usually lies
between 45 and 65 %VO2max [@achten2002; @maunder2018]. The intensity at which
fat oxidation becomes negligible is **Fatmin**: 89 ± 3 %VO2max in
@achten2002 and 90.1 ± 14.1 %VO2max in @cheneviere2009, who defined it as the
second zero of their SIN model.

@achten2002 also defined the **Fatmax zone**, the
range of intensities at which fat oxidation is within 10 % of the peak rate
(mean zone 55–72 %VO2max in their sample). The package therefore needs three
recordings per participant: a resting measurement (the basal state), the
graded MFO test, and a maximal test (or a known VO2max) to express every step
as %VO2max.

## 2. Input data

The three tables shipped with the package are anonymised recordings of one
participant, averaged every 20 s (`step_time = 20`).

```{r data}
head(basal_df)   # resting measurement, 45 records = 15 min
head(MFO_df)     # graded MFO test, 72 records = 8 steps of 3 min
head(VO2max_df)  # maximal graded test
```

Each table must have, at regular intervals of `step_time` seconds, the columns

| Column | Unit | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VO2` | mL/min | substrate oxidation, %VO2max |
| `VCO2` | mL/min | substrate oxidation |
| `RER` | — (VCO2/VO2) | basal window, `RER_cutoff` |
| `HR` | beats/min | heart rate at Fatmax (optional) |

An optional `Load` column (W or km/h) gives Fatmax and the Fatmax zone in load
units. Other columns (`Time`, `BF`, `VE`, `PETCO2`) are ignored. Columns with
other names are mapped with the `col_name_*` arguments of `MFOs()`. Heart rate
never decides which rows or steps are dropped: without HR, `MFO()` warns and
returns `NA` for the heart-rate outputs, and MFO and Fatmax do not change.

## 3. Step by step

`MFO()` runs the whole pipeline in one call. Here each step is rebuilt by
hand, with the same defaults: Frayn equations, 3-min steps, the last 60 s of
each step, P3 fit.

### 3.1 VO2max

VO2max is the highest rolling mean of VO2 in the maximal test over
`vo2max_window` seconds (default 30). With 20-s records a 30-s window is
rounded up to 2 records (40 s). This averaging is a rule of the package.

```{r vo2max}
step_time <- 20
n_vo2max <- ceiling(30 / step_time)                         # 2 records
VO2max <- max(stats::filter(VO2max_df$VO2, rep(1 / n_vo2max, n_vo2max), sides = 1),
              na.rm = TRUE)
c(VO2max = VO2max, instantaneous_max = max(VO2max_df$VO2))
```

### 3.2 Basal window

The first 5 min of the resting recording are discarded. In the rest, the
package takes the 5-min window with the lowest coefficient of variation
(CV = SD / mean) of `cv_var`, here RER. Both durations are rules of the
package.

```{r basal}
window <- 300 / step_time                                   # 15 records = 5 min
rest <- basal_df[-seq_len(window), ]                        # drop the first 5 min
cv <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(rest) - window + 1), function(i) {
  x <- rest$RER[i:(i + window - 1)]
  sd(x) / mean(x)
})
best <- which.min(cv)
basal_window <- rest[best:(best + window - 1), c("VO2", "VCO2", "RER", "HR")]
basal <- colMeans(basal_window)
round(basal, 3)
```

### 3.3 Step averaging

Each 3-min step has 9 records; only the last `steady_state_duration` seconds
(60 s = 3 records) are averaged, as @cheneviere2009 did with the last minute
of each step.

```{r steps}
records_per_step <- 180 / step_time                         # 9
records_steady <- 60 / step_time                            # 3
mfo <- data.frame(MFO_df)
mfo$step <- rep(seq_len(nrow(mfo) %/% records_per_step), each = records_per_step)
position <- ave(mfo$step, mfo$step, FUN = seq_along)
steady <- mfo[position > records_per_step - records_steady, ]
steps <- aggregate(cbind(VO2, VCO2, RER, HR) ~ step, data = steady, FUN = mean)
steps$porc_VO2 <- steps$VO2 / VO2max * 100
round(steps, 2)
```

If the recording ends in the middle of a step, `MFO()` warns with the length
of that incomplete step and drops it, unless `use_incomplete_step = TRUE`.
Here 72 records are exactly 8 steps.

### 3.4 Stoichiometric equation

With VO2 and VCO2 in L/min, the equations of @frayn1983 (the default,
`author = "Frayn"`) are

$$\text{CHO} = 4.55\,\dot{V}\text{CO}_2 - 3.21\,\dot{V}\text{O}_2,
\qquad \text{FAT} = 1.67\,\dot{V}\text{O}_2 - 1.67\,\dot{V}\text{CO}_2 .$$

`author = "Peronnet"` uses the coefficients derived from Table 1 of
@peronnet1991 (4.58519 / 3.22597 and 1.69469 / 1.70130), because the article
prints no equation. `author = "Jeukendrup"` uses the exercise equations
printed by @jeukendrup2005 (Table 5), one CHO equation for 40–50 % and one for
50–75 %VO2max; it needs VO2max and warns for steps outside 40–75 %VO2max.
The same equation is applied to the basal window.

```{r equation}
frayn <- function(VO2, VCO2) {
  data.frame(CHO = 4.55 * VCO2 / 1000 - 3.21 * VO2 / 1000,
             FAT = 1.67 * VO2 / 1000 - 1.67 * VCO2 / 1000)
}
steps <- cbind(steps, frayn(steps$VO2, steps$VCO2))
basal_ox <- frayn(basal[["VO2"]], basal[["VCO2"]])
round(steps[, c("step", "porc_VO2", "RER", "CHO", "FAT")], 3)
round(basal_ox, 3)
```

Energy expenditure (`Kcal` in the output) uses 4 kcal/g CHO and 9 kcal/g fat
with `energy_equivalents = "classic"`, the default in 0.2.x. With `"source"`
it uses the values of the equation's source: 3.8683 / 9.7460 kcal/g
[@peronnet1991], also for Frayn, who gives none, or 3.95 (40–50 %VO2max) /
4.07 (50–75 %VO2max) and 9.75 kcal/g [@jeukendrup2005, Table 5]. MFO and
Fatmax do not depend on this choice.

### 3.5 RER cutoff and negative fat oxidation

With Frayn's coefficients FAT = 1.67 VO2 (1 − RER), so any step with RER > 1
gives a negative fat oxidation, which is an artefact. Two arguments handle
it. `RER_cutoff` removes the steps above a threshold before anything else
(section 6). `negative_FAT` decides what happens to the remaining negative
values: `"truncate"` (default) sets them to 0, `"exclude"` drops the step and
`"keep"` leaves them.

```{r negative}
steps[steps$FAT < 0, c("step", "RER", "FAT")]
steps$FAT[steps$FAT < 0] <- 0                                # negative_FAT = "truncate"
```

By default the basal point is not part of the fit (`include_basal = FALSE`,
section 6).

### 3.6 Curve fit

The default method, P3, fits a third-degree polynomial of FAT on %VO2max.
Fatmax is the root of its derivative that gives the highest FAT within the
measured range, and MFO is the fitted FAT at that root.

```{r fit}
p3 <- lm(FAT ~ porc_VO2 + I(porc_VO2^2) + I(porc_VO2^3), data = steps)
b <- coef(p3)
roots <- Re(polyroot(c(b[2], 2 * b[3], 3 * b[4])))           # FAT'(x) = 0
roots <- roots[roots >= min(steps$porc_VO2) & roots <= max(steps$porc_VO2)]
fat_at <- function(x) predict(p3, newdata = data.frame(porc_VO2 = x))
Fatmax <- roots[which.max(fat_at(roots))]
MFO_hand <- unname(fat_at(Fatmax))
c(MFO = MFO_hand, Fatmax = Fatmax, R2 = summary(p3)$r.squared)
```

### 3.7 Outputs

The Fatmax zone is the range of fitted intensities with FAT ≥ 90 % of MFO
[@achten2002], searched on a grid of 1000 points. The crossover point is the
intensity at which CHO overtakes FAT, interpolated linearly between the two
steps where FAT − CHO changes sign, following the crossover concept of
@brooks1994.
Heart rate at Fatmax is interpolated linearly from the step values.

```{r outputs}
grid <- seq(min(steps$porc_VO2), max(steps$porc_VO2), length.out = 1000)
zone <- range(grid[fat_at(grid) >= 0.9 * MFO_hand])
diff_ox <- steps$FAT - steps$CHO
i <- which(diff(sign(diff_ox)) != 0)[1]
crossover <- approx(diff_ox[i:(i + 1)], steps$porc_VO2[i:(i + 1)], xout = 0)$y
HR_Fatmax <- approx(steps$porc_VO2, steps$HR, xout = Fatmax)$y
round(c(zone_lower = zone[1], zone_upper = zone[2],
        crossover = crossover, HR_Fatmax = HR_Fatmax), 2)
```

The same analysis in one call:

```{r mfo-call}
res <- MFO(step_time = 20, db_MFO = MFO_df, db_basal = basal_df,
           db_graded = VO2max_df, cv_var = "RER", author = "Frayn",
           energy_equivalents = "classic")
hand <- c(VO2max, MFO_hand, Fatmax, zone, crossover, HR_Fatmax,
          basal_ox$CHO, basal_ox$FAT)
package <- c(res$VO2max, res$MFO, res$FAT_MAX, res$FatMax_zone_lower,
             res$FatMax_zone_upper, res$crossover_point, res$FAT_MAX_HR,
             res$x_CHO, res$x_FAT)
all.equal(unname(hand), unname(package))
```

The warning reports the step with RER > 1 that was truncated (3.5); the
message reports the effective VO2max window (3.1). `res$MFO_db` is the step
table that entered the fit: `Step` numbers the steps of the test and `Load` is
the measured load of each step (W). `res$FAT_MAX_load` gives Fatmax in W,
interpolated linearly between steps.

```{r mfo-db, fig.alt = "Fat and carbohydrate oxidation (g/min) against %VO2max for the example participant: observed steps, fitted P3 curves, shaded Fatmax zone and vertical lines at Fatmax and at the crossover point."}
res$MFO_db
res$MFO_plot
```

## 4. Choosing a method

`method` chooses how the peak is located:

- **P3** (default): third-degree polynomial; it can fit an asymmetric curve.
- **P2**: second-degree polynomial; its vertex forces a symmetric curve.
- **MV** (measured values): the step with the highest observed FAT, no fit;
  its resolution is one step, and the Fatmax zone is interpolated linearly
  between steps.
- **MRER**: following @perezmartin2001, as described by @cheneviere2009,
  (1 − RER) and VO2 are fitted as straight lines of intensity and Fatmax is
  the vertex of FAT = 1.7 (1 − RER) VO2, whatever `author` says. It falls back
  to MV with a warning if the vertex is not a maximum inside the measured
  range. Until v0.2.0 the method called `"MRER"` was in fact MV.

To compare them, a small helper runs `MFO()` with the example data and keeps
the warnings as text:

```{r helper}
run_MFO <- function(...) {
  warnings <- character(0)
  out <- withCallingHandlers(
    suppressMessages(MFO(step_time = 20, db_MFO = MFO_df, db_basal = basal_df,
                         db_graded = VO2max_df, cv_var = "RER", author = "Frayn",
                         energy_equivalents = "classic", ...)),
    warning = function(w) {
      warnings <<- c(warnings, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  out$warnings <- warnings
  out
}
```

```{r methods}
methods <- c("P3", "P2", "MV", "MRER")
by_method <- lapply(methods, function(m) run_MFO(method = m))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  method = methods,
  MFO = sapply(by_method, `[[`, "MFO"),
  Fatmax = sapply(by_method, `[[`, "FAT_MAX"),
  zone_lower = sapply(by_method, `[[`, "FatMax_zone_lower"),
  zone_upper = sapply(by_method, `[[`, "FatMax_zone_upper"),
  zone_method = sapply(by_method, `[[`, "FatMax_zone_method"),
  R2 = sapply(by_method, `[[`, "R_squared"),
  RMSE = sapply(by_method, `[[`, "RMSE")
), digits = 3, caption = "MFO (g/min) and Fatmax and zone (%VO2max) by method.")
```

In the comparison by @cheneviere2009, MRER was less accurate than SIN and P3.
Whatever method you choose, look at the observed steps next to the fitted
value: the difference shows how much the fit adds.

## 5. Fat oxidation kinetics with the SIN model

@cheneviere2009 describe the whole curve, normalised to %MFO, with a sine
function of three parameters (their eq. [14]):

$$\%\text{MFO}(x) = \sin\left\{\left[\frac{\pi^{1/s}}{\pi + 2d}\,(Kx + d + t)\right]^{s}\right\},
\qquad K = \frac{\pi}{100},\quad x = \%\dot{V}\text{O}_{2\max}.$$

With d = 0, s = 1 and t = 0 it is a half sine wave with its peak at
50 %VO2max and zeros at 0 and 100 %VO2max. **d** (dilatation) widens (d > 0)
or narrows (d < 0) the curve; **s** (symmetry) skews it: s > 1 is a rightward
asymmetry and 0 < s < 1 a leftward one [@cheneviere2009]; **t** (translation)
shifts the whole curve left (t > 0) or right (t < 0). `MFO_kinetics()` fits
the model by nonlinear least squares directly to the observed steps,
normalised to the highest observed step, without smoothing, as
@cheneviere2009 did. Fatmax_SIN and Fatmin come from closed forms of eq. [14];
Fatmin is the second zero of the curve (set `fatmin_threshold` to use a
proportion of MFO instead).

```{r sin, fig.alt = "Fat oxidation as %MFO against %VO2max: observed steps, the basic SIN curve in grey and the fitted SIN curve in orange between its two zeros; d, s, t, Fatmin and R² in the subtitle."}
kin <- MFO_kinetics(res$MFO_db)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  parameter = c("d", "s", "t"),
  estimate = c(kin$d, kin$s, kin$t),
  std_error = c(kin$d_se, kin$s_se, kin$t_se)
), digits = 3)
round(c(FatMax_SIN = kin$FatMax_SIN, Fatmin = kin$Fatmin, R2 = kin$R_squared), 2)
kin$MFO_kinetics_plot
```

`MFO_kinetics()` fits every row it receives, so the SIN inherits the choices
made in `MFO()`. In this example the last step has RER > 1: truncated to zero
it is a point of the curve, excluded it is not. `RER_cutoff = 1` gives the
selection of @cheneviere2009, who averaged only the steps with RER ≤ 1.0.

```{r sin-sensitivity}
sin_row <- function(label, fit) {
  k <- suppressWarnings(MFO_kinetics(fit$MFO_db))
  data.frame(setting = label, steps = nrow(fit$MFO_db), d = k$d, s = k$s,
             t = k$t, FatMax_SIN = k$FatMax_SIN, Fatmin = k$Fatmin)
}
knitr::kable(rbind(
  sin_row("negative_FAT = \"truncate\"", res),
  sin_row("negative_FAT = \"exclude\"", run_MFO(negative_FAT = "exclude")),
  sin_row("RER_cutoff = 1", run_MFO(RER_cutoff = 1))
), digits = 3, caption = "SIN parameters; Fatmax_SIN and Fatmin in %VO2max.")
```

A single step moves Fatmin by several points here, which is why the setting
must be reported. With fewer than 4 steps the SIN is not fitted
(`convergence = FALSE`); with 4–5 steps it is fitted with a warning, and
6 or more steps are recommended.

## 6. Sensitivity to protocol decisions

### RER cutoff

`RER_cutoff` accepts a number or a name. `"classic"` is 1.00; `"safe"` is
0.95, the threshold @amarogahete2019 recommend to end the test safely;
`"sedentary"` (0.93) and `"trained"` (0.90) are the mean RER at MFO they
found in sedentary and trained people. Lower cutoffs leave fewer steps:

```{r rer-cutoff}
cutoffs <- list(none = NULL, classic = "classic", safe = "safe",
                sedentary = "sedentary", trained = "trained")
by_cutoff <- lapply(cutoffs, function(cut) run_MFO(RER_cutoff = cut))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  RER_cutoff = names(cutoffs),
  steps = sapply(by_cutoff, function(r) nrow(r$MFO_db)),
  MFO = sapply(by_cutoff, `[[`, "MFO"),
  Fatmax = sapply(by_cutoff, `[[`, "FAT_MAX"),
  R2 = sapply(by_cutoff, `[[`, "R_squared"),
  warnings = sapply(by_cutoff, function(r) length(r$warnings)),
  row.names = NULL
), digits = 3)
by_cutoff$trained$warnings
```

With `"trained"` only 4 steps remain and `MFO()` warns that at least
`min_steps` (default 6) are recommended. Its R² of 1 is not a good fit: four
points and four coefficients make the polynomial pass through every point. A
low cutoff only works if the protocol provides enough steps below it.

### Basal point as step 0

`include_basal = TRUE` adds the resting point as step 0 of the fit, and of
the SIN model, which departs from @cheneviere2009. The default `FALSE`
reproduces the results of MFO 0.1.0 and 0.2.0.
<!-- Pending Jorge: attribution of include_basal = TRUE (Montes de Oca et al. 2021, not in SPEC 19); no attribution until then -->

```{r include-basal}
by_basal <- list(`FALSE` = res, `TRUE` = run_MFO(include_basal = TRUE))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  include_basal = names(by_basal),
  rows = sapply(by_basal, function(r) nrow(r$MFO_db)),
  MFO = sapply(by_basal, `[[`, "MFO"),
  Fatmax = sapply(by_basal, `[[`, "FAT_MAX"),
  R2 = sapply(by_basal, `[[`, "R_squared"),
  FatMax_SIN = sapply(by_basal, function(r)
    suppressWarnings(MFO_kinetics(r$MFO_db))$FatMax_SIN),
  row.names = NULL
), digits = 3)
```

## 7. Reporting

The paragraph below is generated from the results of this example; replace
the protocol details (in brackets) with your own. HRmax is taken here as the
highest 20-s heart rate of the maximal test.

```{r report-values}
HRmax <- max(VO2max_df$HR)
final <- run_MFO(HRmax = HRmax)
n_steps <- sum(final$MFO_db$Step != 0)
```

```{r report, results = "asis", echo = FALSE}
paragraph <- sprintf(paste(
  "Substrate oxidation was computed from the mean VO2 and VCO2 of the last %d s",
  "of each %d-min step with the equations of Frayn (1983), with urinary nitrogen",
  "set to zero. VO2max (%.0f mL/min) was the highest %d-s rolling mean of VO2 in",
  "the maximal test. The resting value was the mean of the 5-min window with the",
  "lowest coefficient of variation of RER after discarding the first 5 min.",
  "Negative fat oxidation rates (RER > 1) were set to zero and the resting point",
  "was not included in the fit. MFO and Fatmax were determined with a",
  "third-degree polynomial of fat oxidation on %%VO2max fitted to %d steps",
  "(R² = %.2f). The Fatmax zone was defined as the intensities eliciting at least",
  "90%% of MFO (Achten et al., 2002). Fat oxidation kinetics were described with",
  "the SIN model (Chenevière et al., 2009). MFO was %.2f g/min at %.1f%% VO2max",
  "(%.0f bpm, %.1f%% HRmax; Fatmax zone %.1f–%.1f%% VO2max); the SIN parameters",
  "were d = %.2f, s = %.2f and t = %.2f, with Fatmin at %.1f%% VO2max. Analyses",
  "were run with the R package MFO, version %s, [protocol: ergometer, initial",
  "load and increment, fasting and pre-test conditions]."),
  60, 3, final$VO2max, final$VO2max_window, n_steps, final$R_squared,
  final$MFO, final$FAT_MAX, final$FAT_MAX_HR, final$FAT_MAX_porcHRmax,
  final$FatMax_zone_lower, final$FatMax_zone_upper, kin$d, kin$s, kin$t,
  kin$Fatmin, as.character(utils::packageVersion("MFO")))
cat("> ", paragraph, "\n")
```

Add MFO relative to body mass or fat-free mass when you have them
(`body_mass`, `fat_free_mass`). Also report the day-to-day error of the
measure when you interpret individual values: in @chrzanowski2020 (n = 99)
the coefficient of variation was 21 % for MFO and 26 % for Fatmax, and in
@croci2014 (n = 15) the CV of Fatmax was 16.4 % with SIN, 18.6 % with P3 and
20.8 % with MV.

## 8. Batch processing with `MFOs()`

`MFOs()` applies the same analysis to many participants and returns one row
per participant. With `from = "folder"` each participant has a subfolder
with three xlsx files; with `from = "files"` each participant has one xlsx
file with three sheets. The example builds two participants in a temporary
folder: P01 is the example data and P02 the same data with VO2 and VCO2
scaled by 1.1 (same RER), so that the two rows differ.

```{r batch-data}
root <- file.path(tempdir(), "mfo-batch")
dir.create(root, showWarnings = FALSE)
scale_gas <- function(db, k) transform(db, VO2 = VO2 * k, VCO2 = VCO2 * k)
for (id in c("P01", "P02")) {
  k <- if (id == "P01") 1 else 1.1
  dir.create(file.path(root, id), showWarnings = FALSE)
  openxlsx::write.xlsx(scale_gas(basal_df, k), file.path(root, id, "basal_df.xlsx"))
  openxlsx::write.xlsx(scale_gas(MFO_df, k), file.path(root, id, "MFO_df.xlsx"))
  openxlsx::write.xlsx(scale_gas(VO2max_df, k), file.path(root, id, "VO2max_df.xlsx"))
}
list.files(root, recursive = TRUE)
```

`save_plot` and `save_result` write the plots and the summary table to the
working directory; they are switched off here. Every warning is repeated with
the participant ID in front.

```{r batch}
batch <- MFOs(from = "folder", path = root,
              db_basal_name = "basal_df", db_MFO_name = "MFO_df",
              db_graded_name = "VO2max_df", step_time = 20, cv_var = "RER",
              author = "Frayn", energy_equivalents = "classic",
              save_plot = FALSE, save_result = FALSE)
knitr::kable(batch[, c("ID", "MFO_g_min", "FAT_MAX_perVO2max", "VO2max",
                       "FatMax_zone_lower", "FatMax_zone_upper", "d", "s", "t",
                       "Fatmin")], digits = 3)
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
```

## References
